:::{#rem-design-matrix-products}
#### Products with the design matrix

The product $\mX\vcoef$ collects the values $\tp{\vx_i}\vcoef$
for all $n$ observations into a single $n \times 1$ vector:

$$
\mX\vcoef =
\begin{bmatrix}
\tp{\vx_1}\vcoef \\
\vdots \\
\tp{\vx_n}\vcoef
\end{bmatrix}
$$

For example, take the rank-$2$ matrix from @exm-rank as $\mX$,
with $n = 3$ observations and $p = 2$ columns:
an intercept column and one covariate.
With $\vcoef = (1, 2)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mX\vcoef
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix $\tp{\mX}\mX$ is $p \times p$ and symmetric,
since $\tp{(\tp{\mX}\mX)} = \tp{\mX}\,\tp{(\tp{\mX})} = \tp{\mX}\mX$
(@thm-transpose-product).
When $\tp{\mX}\mX$ is invertible,
it appears in the OLS estimator $\hvcoef = (\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\tp{\mX}\vy$.

:::
